questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: She told me that she is tired.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, if the reporting verb is in the past tense, the verb in the noun clause shifts back one tense (is -> was). (Bahasa Indonesia: Dalam reported speech, jika kata kerja pelapor dalam bentuk lampau, kata kerja di dalam anak kalimat bergeser satu bentuk ke belakang (is -> was).)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: I am used to wake up early.
questions.explanation: The expression 'be used to' is followed by a gerund (V-ing) because 'to' functions as a preposition here. (Bahasa Indonesia: Ungkapan 'be used to' diikuti oleh gerund (V-ing) karena 'to' berfungsi sebagai preposisi di sini.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: He gave me an advice.
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is an uncountable noun and cannot be used with 'an'. Use 'some advice' or 'a piece of advice'. (Bahasa Indonesia: 'Advice' adalah kata benda yang tidak dapat dihitung dan tidak dapat digunakan dengan 'an'. Gunakan 'some advice' atau 'a piece of advice'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: She is the woman which won the prize.
questions.explanation: Use 'who' to refer to people in relative clauses, not 'which'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Gunakan 'who' untuk merujuk pada orang dalam relative clauses, bukan 'which'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: She enjoys to read novels.
questions.explanation: The verb 'enjoy' is always followed by a gerund (V-ing), not an infinitive. (Bahasa Indonesia: Kata kerja 'enjoy' selalu diikuti oleh gerund (V-ing), bukan infinitive.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: The window was broke by the ball.
questions.explanation: The passive voice requires the past participle (V3). The past participle of 'break' is 'broken'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Kalimat pasif memerlukan past participle (V3). Past participle dari 'break' adalah 'broken'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: By the time we arrived, the movie already started.
questions.explanation: Use the past perfect tense ('had' + V3) for an action completed before another action in the past. (Bahasa Indonesia: Gunakan past perfect tense ('had' + V3) untuk tindakan yang selesai sebelum tindakan lain di masa lampau.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: She is more taller than her sister.
questions.explanation: For one-syllable adjectives, add '-er' to form the comparative. Do not use 'more' with '-er'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Untuk kata sifat satu suku kata, tambahkan '-er' untuk membentuk komparatif. Jangan gunakan 'more' dengan '-er'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: She has less friends than me.
questions.explanation: Use 'fewer' for countable nouns (friends) and 'less' for uncountable nouns. (Bahasa Indonesia: Gunakan 'fewer' untuk kata benda yang dapat dihitung (friends) dan 'less' untuk kata benda yang tidak dapat dihitung.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: Neither John nor his friends is coming.
questions.explanation: With 'neither... nor...', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'Friends' is plural, so use 'are'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Dengan 'neither... nor...', kata kerja setuju dengan subjek yang paling dekat dengannya. 'Friends' adalah jamak, jadi gunakan 'are'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: There is many apples in the basket.
questions.explanation: 'Apples' is a plural countable noun, so it requires the plural verb 'are'. (Bahasa Indonesia: 'Apples' adalah kata benda jamak yang dapat dihitung, sehingga memerlukan kata kerja jamak 'are'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: If it will rain, we will cancel the trip.
questions.explanation: In Conditional Type 1, the if-clause uses the simple present tense, not the future tense. (Bahasa Indonesia: Dalam Conditional Type 1, anak kalimat if menggunakan simple present tense, bukan future tense.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: Neither of the boys are coming to the party.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular and requires a singular verb ('is'), even when followed by 'of the + plural noun'. (Bahasa Indonesia: 'Neither' adalah tunggal dan memerlukan kata kerja tunggal ('is'), bahkan ketika diikuti oleh 'of the + kata benda jamak'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: The homework was did by the students.
questions.explanation: The passive voice requires the past participle (V3). The past participle of 'do' is 'done'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Kalimat pasif memerlukan past participle (V3). Past participle dari 'do' adalah 'done'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: He is the most smartest student in class.
questions.explanation: Do not use 'most' with adjectives that already have the '-est' suffix. Use 'the smartest'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Jangan gunakan 'most' dengan kata sifat yang sudah memiliki akhiran '-est'. Gunakan 'the smartest'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: The news are very shocking today.
questions.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb, despite ending in 's'. (Bahasa Indonesia: 'News' adalah kata benda yang tidak dapat dihitung dan selalu menggunakan kata kerja tunggal, meskipun berakhiran 's'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: This is the most unique phenomenon.
questions.explanation: 'Unique' is an absolute adjective and does not take comparative or superlative forms like 'most'. (Bahasa Indonesia: 'Unique' adalah kata sifat absolut dan tidak mengambil bentuk komparatif atau superlatif seperti 'most'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: The book are on the table.
questions.explanation: Singular subjects like 'the book' require the singular verb 'is'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Subjek tunggal seperti 'the book' memerlukan kata kerja tunggal 'is'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: She is interested on learning Spanish.
questions.explanation: The correct adjective-preposition collocation is 'interested in', not 'interested on'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Kolokasi kata sifat-preposisi yang benar adalah 'interested in', bukan 'interested on'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: The cake was eat by the dog.
questions.explanation: The passive voice requires the past participle (V3). The past participle of 'eat' is 'eaten'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Kalimat pasif memerlukan past participle (V3). Past participle dari 'eat' adalah 'eaten'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: The car was stole yesterday.
questions.explanation: The passive voice structure is 'be' + past participle (V3). The past participle of 'steal' is 'stolen'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Struktur kalimat pasif adalah 'be' + past participle (V3). Past participle dari 'steal' adalah 'stolen'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: He should has studied harder for the exam.
questions.explanation: Modal verbs are always followed by the base form 'have', never 'has' or 'had'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Kata kerja modal selalu diikuti oleh bentuk dasar 'have', tidak pernah 'has' atau 'had'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: I look forward to see you.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'look forward to' is always followed by a gerund (V-ing), not an infinitive. (Bahasa Indonesia: Frasa 'look forward to' selalu diikuti oleh gerund (V-ing), bukan infinitive.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: I will call you when I will arrive.
questions.explanation: In time clauses referring to the future, use the simple present tense, not the future tense. (Bahasa Indonesia: Dalam time clauses yang merujuk pada masa depan, gunakan simple present tense, bukan future tense.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: I wish I can fly.
questions.explanation: To express a wish about ability in the present, use 'could' after 'wish'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Untuk mengekspresikan harapan tentang kemampuan di masa kini, gunakan 'could' setelah 'wish'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: He is good in playing chess.
questions.explanation: The correct collocation is 'good at' something, not 'good in'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Kolokasi yang benar adalah 'good at' sesuatu, bukan 'good in'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: She said that she will come tomorrow.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'will' changes to 'would' when the reporting verb is in the past tense. (Bahasa Indonesia: Dalam reported speech, 'will' berubah menjadi 'would' ketika kata kerja pelapor dalam bentuk lampau.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: We have lived here since five years.
questions.explanation: Use 'for' to indicate a duration of time, and 'since' for a specific starting point. (Bahasa Indonesia: Gunakan 'for' untuk menunjukkan durasi waktu, dan 'since' untuk titik awal waktu yang spesifik.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: They is going to the market right now.
questions.explanation: Plural subjects like 'they' require the plural verb 'are' in the present continuous tense. (Bahasa Indonesia: Subjek jamak seperti 'they' memerlukan kata kerja jamak 'are' dalam present continuous tense.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: I have went to Paris last year.
questions.explanation: The present perfect tense requires 'have/has' + past participle (V3). The past participle of 'go' is 'gone'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Present perfect tense memerlukan 'have/has' + past participle (V3). Past participle dari 'go' adalah 'gone'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: I have never saw such a beautiful painting.
questions.explanation: The present perfect tense uses 'have/has' + past participle (V3). The past participle of 'see' is 'seen'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Present perfect tense menggunakan 'have/has' + past participle (V3). Past participle dari 'see' adalah 'seen'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: If I had knew, I would have told you.
questions.explanation: Conditional Type 3 uses 'had' + past participle (V3) in the if-clause. The past participle of 'know' is 'known'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Conditional Type 3 menggunakan 'had' + past participle (V3) di dalam anak kalimat if. Past participle dari 'know' adalah 'known'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: She don't like coffee in the morning.
questions.explanation: In Simple Present Tense, third person singular subjects (he, she, it) require 'does not' or 'doesn't' + base verb. (Bahasa Indonesia: Dalam Simple Present Tense, subjek orang ketiga tunggal (he, she, it) memerlukan 'does not' atau 'doesn't' + kata kerja dasar.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: They have been married since ten years.
questions.explanation: Use 'for' to indicate a duration of time (ten years), and 'since' for a specific starting point. (Bahasa Indonesia: Gunakan 'for' untuk menunjukkan durasi waktu (ten years), dan 'since' untuk titik awal waktu yang spesifik.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: He is afraid from spiders.
questions.explanation: The correct adjective-preposition collocation is 'afraid of', not 'afraid from'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Kolokasi kata sifat-preposisi yang benar adalah 'afraid of', bukan 'afraid from'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: The teacher, along with her students, are going to the museum.
questions.explanation: Phrases like 'along with' do not change the number of the subject. The main subject 'teacher' is singular. (Bahasa Indonesia: Frasa seperti 'along with' tidak mengubah jumlah subjek. Subjek utama 'teacher' adalah tunggal.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: If I was you, I would study harder.
questions.explanation: In Conditional Type 2, 'were' is used for all subjects (including I, he, she, it) in the if-clause. (Bahasa Indonesia: Dalam Conditional Type 2, 'were' digunakan untuk semua subjek (termasuk I, he, she, it) di dalam anak kalimat if.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: She is more smarter than her classmates.
questions.explanation: Do not use 'more' with adjectives that already have the '-er' comparative suffix. (Bahasa Indonesia: Jangan gunakan 'more' dengan kata sifat yang sudah memiliki akhiran komparatif '-er'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: I would rather stay at home than to go out.
questions.explanation: The structure 'would rather... than...' is followed by the base form of the verb without 'to'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Struktur 'would rather... than...' diikuti oleh bentuk dasar kata kerja tanpa 'to'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: I am looking forward to meet you.
questions.explanation: 'Look forward to' is a phrasal verb where 'to' is a preposition, so it must be followed by a gerund (V-ing). (Bahasa Indonesia: 'Look forward to' adalah phrasal verb di mana 'to' adalah preposisi, sehingga harus diikuti oleh gerund (V-ing).)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: We have much books in the library.
questions.explanation: Use 'many' for countable plural nouns (books) and 'much' for uncountable nouns. (Bahasa Indonesia: Gunakan 'many' untuk kata benda jamak yang dapat dihitung (books) dan 'much' untuk kata benda yang tidak dapat dihitung.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: We must finishing the project today.
questions.explanation: Modal verbs are always followed by the base form of the verb (V1). (Bahasa Indonesia: Kata kerja modal selalu diikuti oleh bentuk dasar kata kerja (V1).)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: She asked me where do I live.
questions.explanation: In reported questions, the word order is subject + verb, and the tense shifts to the past. (Bahasa Indonesia: Dalam pertanyaan reported speech, urutan katanya adalah subjek + kata kerja, dan tense bergeser ke bentuk lampau.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: He didn't went to school yesterday.
questions.explanation: After 'didn't', the main verb must be in its base form (V1). (Bahasa Indonesia: Setelah 'didn't', kata kerja utama harus dalam bentuk dasar (V1).)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: The man which lives next door is a doctor.
questions.explanation: Use 'who' for people, not 'which'. 'Which' is used for things or animals. (Bahasa Indonesia: Gunakan 'who' untuk orang, bukan 'which'. 'Which' digunakan untuk benda atau hewan.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: He can speaks English fluently.
questions.explanation: Modal verbs (can, could, should, must) are always followed by the base form of the verb without 'to' or 's'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Kata kerja modal (can, could, should, must) selalu diikuti oleh bentuk dasar kata kerja tanpa 'to' atau 's'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: He runs more faster than his brother.
questions.explanation: Do not use 'more' with comparative adjectives that already end in '-er'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Jangan gunakan 'more' dengan kata sifat komparatif yang sudah berakhiran '-er'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: The children is playing in the park.
questions.explanation: 'Children' is the plural form of 'child', so it requires the plural verb 'are'. (Bahasa Indonesia: 'Children' adalah bentuk jamak dari 'child', sehingga memerlukan kata kerja jamak 'are'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: I wish I have a million dollars.
questions.explanation: To express a wish about the present, use the past tense form after 'wish'. (Bahasa Indonesia: Untuk mengekspresikan harapan tentang masa kini, gunakan bentuk past tense setelah 'wish'.)

questions.question: Click the incorrect word or phrase and type the correct one.
questions.sentence: He didn't knew the answer.
questions.explanation: After the auxiliary 'did' or 'didn't', the main verb must be in its base form (V1). (Bahasa Indonesia: Setelah kata bantu 'did' atau 'didn't', kata kerja utama harus dalam bentuk dasar (V1).)
